To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a Gaussian Markov model is a good approximation for the average field on a mirror in a Fabry-Perot resonator when waves are refract repeatedly by the same "frozen" turbulence, but the Gaussian Markov model does not describe the angular distribution of radiation.

the angular divergence of the transmitted wave field in the case of repeated transmission through a medium with random scatterers can be described by a Gaussian distribution, and that the angular divergence in the case of multiple transmission of a wave across a medium with turbulent perturbations is described by the same Gaussian distribution.
the angular divergence of the radiation transmitted by a random medium can be predicted by a Gaussian Markov process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the propagation of waves through a turbulent medium.
the problem of the multiple transmission of waves across an optically active medium with random scattering and angular divergence of the radiation in a Fabrey–Perot resonators.
the propagation of light waves through a random medium with angular divergence in the Fabry–Perots resonators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Markovian approach is a good tool to model the average behavior of light in a turbulent medium.
, in the presence of turbulence, the angular divergence of the radiation in a Fabroy-Perot resonator can be reduced by decreasing the mirror reflectivity.
a Gaussian Markov process is an excellent model for the description of the average properties of a wave field in a turbulent medium, but it is not suitable for the description of its fluctuations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gaussian Markova approximation gives good results when the angular divergence is small and the transmission of radiation is large.
a Gaussian Markov model can be applied in a wide range of parameters of a medium with random scatterers.

, when a beam is refracted by random scattering centers and the angular divergence of the radiation increases in a Fabry-Perot resonator with each reflection, a Gaussian Markov model of turbulence is applicable to the description of the average field characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the results obtained by the Gaussian Markov model are applicable to the description of the angular divergence and distribution of the field in a Fabry-Perot resonator.
the Gaussian Markof approximation can be applied to the analysis of the angular distribution of radiation transmitted by the medium with random scatterers.
the Gaussian Markoff approximation describes satisfactorilly the average characteristics of the radiation transmitted by the turbulent medium.
